evidence.requirements: Almost every requirement is met. The start page has the heading, the links, the search over alternative names, the Family select and the '<n> cartridges' count (index.html:14-31, app.js:15-25, list.jpg). The detail view has all the facts, the water capacity with its source link, grouped Symbol/Value/Unit tables with tolerances inline ('39.62 -0.2'), Print, 'All cartridges', and hash routes that survive a reload (app.js:77-122). The drawing has every required dimension and the title block (drawing.js:194-312). Missing values are named in a figcaption (geometry.js:165-208). Print fits one A4 page with a header and a footer (print.css, print-308_win.jpg). Partly met: (1) 'drawing at full width' in print. The SVG box is full width, but the part takes about 60% of it and the fixed 44 mm title block (TITLE_W, drawing.js:19) fills the rest (print-308_win.jpg). (2) 'Scales to a phone' is handled in code (titleBelow, app.js:53) and tested, but no phone screenshot was provided, so I could not check it visually. (3) Angle rows repeat the degree sign: the Value '40°' is followed by a Unit '°' (format.js:40, detail-308_win.jpg). (4) Whether the agent followed the brief's Process section cannot be checked from the repo.
evidence.correctness: The geometry follows the rules closely. Rim type matches rule 1 (geometry.js:11-16). The chamfer uses min(f·tanβ, R1/4) (149). The rimfire half-round has radius min(R/2, (R1-P1)/2) with its outermost point at R1/2 (152-160). The groove floor and ramp follow rule 3. The belt ramp rises at δ (dz = dr/tanδ) to R3/2, then runs to E (181-184). Bottleneck and straight bodies are handled, and the shoulder is drawn through the published points, with r1 min and r2 fillets (202-211). For the bullet, s, k and m match every case in the table (84-86). The tangent-ogive ρ and its centre are correct, and the arc ends exactly at m/2 (96-103). Rounded noses are a quarter ellipse, flat and SWC noses a cone. A heeled case uses H2 for the exposed bullet and H2-2tb for the heel (82, 123). The tn/tb walls blend across the shoulder. w is the max() from rule 8, and the primer pocket sizes are right (216-233). Outlines match the references in proportion: 308 Win. (rounded shoulder, ogive with meplat), 300 Win. Mag. (belt), 9 mm Luger (taper plus round nose), 22 LR (rounded rim, heel line at the mouth, drawing.js:132). Label values match the tables, and angles show as 40° or 10°58'0". Print fits one page (print-308_win.jpg, print.test.js:67-79). Minor points: the inner wall is offset radially, not along the surface normal. On straight cases tb→tn is blended from w to the bullet base, which is an interpretation of the rule. The α arc's vertex floats above the body, off the extended shoulder line, which is unconventional though it does show the included angle (drawing.js:258-292).
evidence.security: All HTML is built through esc() for names, facts, table cells and SVG text (app.js:8,17-50; drawing.js:22,189,309,315). The data is a JSON.parse of an embedded string (data.js:31). There is no eval, Function or remote fetch. The only external URLs are the record's capacity source links, which only load when the user clicks them, and an e2e test asserts that the page makes no outside requests (browse.test.js:52-53).
evidence.code_quality: The structure is clear: data, format, geometry, drawing and app are separate modules with single responsibilities (README.md:7). Geometry is pure and returns notes for missing values, and drawing returns its label boxes and segments so tests can inspect them. The naming follows the C.I.P. symbols. Weaknesses: build() in drawing.js is a 250-line function with many magic constants. The label placer brute-forces a spiral of about 18,000 candidate offsets, checked against every segment (drawing.js:170-183). Some lines are very dense one-liners (drawing.js:36, 162).
evidence.tests: The unit tests check the geometry rules against hand-computed values: the chamfer and its R1/4 cap, groove points, the belt ramp at δ, the rimmed step, the rimfire half-round, fillets, the straight case, walls, w, pocket sizes, ogive ρ, seating depth, k and m per shape, the heeled bullet, and the missing-value notes (geometry.test.js). Formatting, symbols, units, tolerances and the rule that every field is shown exactly once are covered (format.test.js). The e2e tests run over both file:// and HTTP. They cover search, filter, count, routing, reload and back navigation, the detail facts and tables, the Print button, label overlap measured in the real DOM for all 25 records, one A4 page per record, dark/light, and phone width (e2e/*.test.js). Gaps: rounded, flat and SWC nose coordinates are not asserted. The section hatch and inner line are only lightly checked. Nothing checks print legibility (font size), and nothing checks rebated geometry beyond the classification.
evidence.ux_design: The information hierarchy is good: name, then the facts grid, then the drawing, then grouped tables in a dense 3-column grid with right-aligned tabular numbers (detail-308_win.jpg). But the drawing is small on desktop: the 308 Win. sits at 1.7:1 in roughly the left 55% of the figure. Because the label font and the title block are fixed in mm, small cartridges are swamped: on 22 LR and 9 mm Luger the title block is as large as the cartridge and the labels dwarf the part (detail-22_long_rifle.jpg, detail-9_mm_luger.jpg). The doubled '°' in angle rows adds noise. Print is clean, black on white and one page, but the tables are 6.5 pt (print-308_win.jpg). There are no dark-mode screenshots to judge dark on screen.
evidence.accessibility: The SVG has role=img, aria-label '<name> drawing', a <title> and a <desc> (drawing.js:317-318). Tables have captions, th scope=col and th scope=row (app.js:45-46). The search and select have real labels (index.html:16-19), and the count has role=status. Focus moves to the h1 on navigation (app.js:121), and focus-visible outlines are defined (style.css:39). Muted text #59636d on #fbfbf9 has adequate contrast. Gaps: the text alternative only describes the drawing generally, though the tables carry every value. The hidden h1 focus outline is removed; that is acceptable for programmatic focus.
evidence.simplicity: There are no runtime dependencies and one dev dependency (playwright-core). About 900 lines of app JS is proportionate to the drawing rules. The generic collision-search label placer is heavier than a fixed layout would need, but it is what guarantees no overlaps.
evidence.maintainability: There is a README with serve and test commands, plus OpenSpec specs per capability (openspec/specs/*), a lockfile, and readable module boundaries. Missing: there is no CI configuration, no ADRs or decision log, and no engines field or .nvmrc pinning Node 22. The e2e runner hard-codes a cached Chromium path ~/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-*/chrome-linux64 (helpers.js:10-15). playwright-core does not download that browser, and the README does not say how to install it, which is an undocumented manual step. There is no versioning or release approach beyond version 1.0.0 in package.json.
evidence.visual_design: The design is calm and technical: a neutral palette, small uppercase muted labels, a monospace drawing font, consistent hairline table rules, and the same structure on every page (all detail-*.jpg). The drawing's line weights are crisp and it has a proper dash-dot centre line and hatching. The weak spot is composition: the bold oversized mono title block and the 3 mm labels outweigh small parts (detail-22_long_rifle.jpg), and the bullet tint in the section is very faint.
evidence.layout: The page order is right: title, facts, drawing, then the tables. The tables pack into an auto-fill grid, and there is no clipping or overlap in any screenshot. But in the drawing frame the cartridge occupies a minority of the area, with a large empty region above right on 308 Win. and 300 Win. Mag., while the title block sits low right. Short sections (Collar, Miscellaneous) leave big gaps in the table grid. In print the drawing also uses only about 60% of the width (print-308_win.jpg).
evidence.usability: Tasks take few steps: type to filter (alternative names work, '7,62 x 51' finds 308 Win.), select a family, click a name, and the address can be bookmarked. Back keeps the filter state (browse.test.js:39-41). An unknown address shows 'Cartridge not found' with a way back. Print is one click and needs no setup. Missing values are explained next to the drawing. No error states are needed beyond these.
evidence.reception: Reloaders and engineers would trust the faithful data, correct symbols, inline tolerances and a true-to-scale drawing with C.I.P.-style dimensioning that is close to the OpenBallistics references. The small drawing with oversized labels on small cartridges and the doubled degree units take away some polish. Overall it looks like a credible reference people would reuse.

unmet_requirements: Print: 'drawing at full width' is only partly met; the part uses about 60% of the page width beside a fixed 44 mm title block (print-308_win.jpg)
Angle rows show the degree sign twice: Value '40°' plus Unit '°' (format.js:40)
No phone-width screenshot was provided, so phone scaling could only be checked in code and tests
Maintainability: no CI, no ADRs, no pinned Node version, and an undocumented Chromium install for the e2e tests (helpers.js:10-15)
strengths: The geometry follows the brief's rules precisely: rim types, chamfer cap, rimfire half-round, groove, belt ramp at δ, shoulder fillets, a correct tangent ogive, the heeled bullet, walls, solid head and primer pocket. Outlines match the reference drawings and every missing value is named.

Strong automated tests run over both file:// and HTTP: rule-level unit tests with hand-computed values, real-DOM checks that no label overlaps anything for all 25 records, one A4 page per record, no external requests, and dark/light.
Clean, safe, dependency-free implementation with escaped rendering, hash routing that survives a reload, and a dense, well-labelled table layout suited to a technical audience.
issues: Drawing composition: the part is small inside its frame on screen and in print. The fixed-size labels and the 44 mm title block dominate small cartridges (22 LR, 9 mm Luger), and the print drawing does not use the full page width.
Maintainability gaps: no CI pipeline, no ADRs, no Node version pinning, and e2e tests that need a hard-coded, undocumented Chromium cache path.

Display details: the degree sign is duplicated in angle rows, print tables are 6.5 pt, the α annotation is unconventional (vertex floating above the body), and the bullet tint in the section is faint.
review.verdict: This is a faithful, well-tested implementation: the drawing rules are followed almost to the letter, labels never overlap, and the printout is one clean A4 page. Before publishing, the drawing needs to be enlarged and balanced against its labels and title block, and CI and setup documentation should be added.
